title: Rate-limit password reset requests
user: A user who asks for more than five password resets in an hour sees a wait message instead of another email. As written the limit never resets, because the counter key has no expiry.

behaviors.before: Any number of reset emails per hour
behaviors.after: The sixth request in an hour is refused
behaviors.verified: npm test -- reset-limiter: 4 passing, including 'refuses the sixth request'
behaviors.detail: The limiter counts requests per email in the cache and refuses at six. The controller checks the limiter before it queues the email, so a refused request sends nothing.

behaviors.after: The form shows how long to wait
behaviors.why: The wait message depends on a translation bundle that is only built in CI, and I could not run that job locally.
behaviors.detail: The controller returns 429 with a retry-after header and the form reads it into the message. Any other error keeps the existing generic text.

behaviors.before: An unused legacy reset endpoint ships
behaviors.verified: rg -F 'legacy-reset' src/ test/ returned nothing; npm run build passes
behaviors.detail: The route was never registered after the router rewrite, so nothing reached it.

flows.name: User requests a password reset
steps: Open the sign-in page and choose Forgot password
Submit the same email six times within an hour
The sixth submit shows the wait message and sends no email

flows.name: Operator reads the audit log
flows.effect: Each refused request logs the email hash and the retry time, so support can see why a user got no email.

changed_files: Counts reset requests per email and refuses at six
The count lives beside the token store so a restart does not clear it
Asks the limiter before queueing the email
The controller is the one place every reset request passes through
Leaving it is a second reset path with no limiter on it
Shows the wait message on a 429 response
A bare 429 reads as a broken form, so the wait has to be named

blockers.title: The counter key never expires, so the limit never resets
blockers.detail: Line 31 writes the count with cache.set(key, n) and no TTL. After six requests the user is refused forever. Proven with a unit test that advances the clock by two hours and still gets a refusal. Pass the window length as the TTL on every write.

nonBlockers.title: Email is compared case-sensitively
nonBlockers.detail: The key is built from the raw email, so User@example.com and user@example.com get separate counters and the limit is six per spelling. Lowercase the email before building the key, as reset-controller.ts:42 already does for the lookup.
